investigacion.base:
I couldn't open the resolution sources' live pages directly, so the numbers below come from search snippets and mirror sites.

**Current status (as of about Sep 29, 2026)**
- Cboe shows VIX spot at $16.03 (as of September 29, 2026), down 0.04. Yahoo's ^VIX history page last showed a close on September 29 at 3:15:01 PM CDT, but the snippet didn't include the values.
- September 2026 daily data from Investing.com: the monthly intraday high was 18.94 on Sep 16, and there was also an 18.17 high on Sep 10 and Sep 14. On Sep 25 VIX closed at 14.87 (high 15.94, low 14.68). The lowest September intraday level was 13.80 on Sep 4. (table)
- The question says August's high was 18.43 (Aug 5). So VIX has stayed roughly between 14 and 19 since late summer.
- The 52-week high is 35.30, set on 03/09/26, and the 52-week low was 13.38 on 12/24/25.
- Other volatility gauges on Sep 22: the 3-month VIX (VIX3M) closed at 17.61 and the Nasdaq-100 VIX (VXN) at 20.18. VIX3M sitting above VIX means the futures curve is in normal upward-sloping "contango", so markets don't expect a near-term spike.
- I didn't find the Metaculus page content or any prediction-market prices.

**Recent news**
- CNBC, Sep 10: September and October are typically among the months when the VIX jumps the most. Nomura's McElligott pointed to the U.S. midterms, rate risk, hawkish central banks and an escalation in Middle East hostilities as reasons for hedging.
- Demand for protection is high: the VIX three-month call skew — is in the 91st percentile of its historical range. That means options betting on a volatility jump are expensive.
- On the other hand, VIX and the MOVE bond-volatility index are near their 10-year averages, and credit spreads are historically tight .

**Scheduled events before Dec 24 (typical calendar; not checked against 2026 schedules)**
- Monthly jobs reports and CPI releases.
- Big-tech Q3 earnings in late October.
- U.S. midterm elections on Nov 3, 2026.
- FOMC meetings, likely around late October and mid-December.
- Monthly VIX options expirations and the December quarterly options expiration.

**Rough base rates** (from memory, approximate): highest intraday VIX over roughly Oct 1–Dec 24 each year:

| Year | Approx. high | When / cause |
|---|---|---|
| 2017 | ~14 | |
| 2018 | ~36 | Dec 24 |
| 2019 | ~21 | |
| 2020 | ~41 | Late Oct, election |
| 2021 | ~35 | Omicron |
| 2022 | ~34 | |
| 2023 | ~23 | |
| 2024 | ~28 | Dec 18 FOMC |
| 2025 | ~28–29 | |

- Median is roughly 28.
- The maximum over the whole quarter nearly always ends up well above the starting spot level, usually 1.3–2x. Starting from about 16 now, that means roughly 20–30.
- Midterm-election years tend to see volatility build up to the election and fall afterwards.

**Status quo:** Nothing has resolved yet. If VIX just stayed where it is, the answer would be around 16–19. Any geopolitical or rate shock could push it into the high 20s or 30s.

criterios:
This question will resolve as the highest "High" value of ^VIX for any date between October 1, 2026, and December 24, 2026 (inclusive), according to [Yahoo! Finance](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/history/).

For example, in the month of August 2026, the highest intraday value for ^VIX was 18.43 (on August 5).

(b) **If nothing changed:** A VIX near its current level of 16 would produce a high of roughly 16–18.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** Recent trading has been subdued but variable; a period high around 19–23 would be plausible.

(d) **Experts and markets:** The upward-sloping VIX term structure suggests no immediate volatility spike is expected, while expensive protection and upcoming elections point to meaningful upside risk. I found no reliable market forecast for this specific maximum.

(e) **Unexpected low outcome:** A sustained, unusually calm rally could keep the high around 14–17.

(f) **Unexpected high outcome:** A major geopolitical or financial shock could push the VIX above 40.

(a) **Time left:** About 12 weeks, covering roughly 60 trading days from Oct 1 to Dec 24, 2026. The answer will be known on Dec 24.

(b) **If nothing changed:** VIX is near 16, and its normal daily swings have produced monthly highs of about 18–19 in August and September. So the quarter's high would land around 18–19.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** The recent range is 14–19, with no strong upward drift. A calm continuation still usually produces at least one flare-up to about 20–22 over 60 trading days.

(d) **Experts and markets:**
- VIX3M is above spot, so the futures curve slopes upward and markets price only modest near-term stress.
- Upside call skew is expensive (91st percentile), which shows hedging demand.
- The main event risks are the Nov 3 midterms, late-October and December FOMC meetings, geopolitics and big-tech earnings.
- Base rate: the quarter's maximum has typically been 1.3–1.8x the starting level, with a median near 1.5x. From 16, that implies about 24.
- In recent years with similar starting levels, the highs were about 21 (2019), 23 (2023), 28 (2024) and 29 (2025).

(e) **Low-outcome scenario:** A 2017-style grind higher with benign inflation data, a smooth election and a dovish Fed. VIX stays at 12–16, and the highest print is about 16.5–17.5.

(f) **High-outcome scenario:** A disputed midterm result, a Middle East escalation hitting oil, a hawkish shock, or an AI/tech earnings unwind. Any of these could send VIX into the 30s–40s intraday, as in December 2018 (~36) or October 2020 (~41).
